ask: GLSL 450 compute. reduce.comp: parallel reduction of a float array to a sum using shared memory, local_size_x = 256, tree reduction with barriers, workgroup partial sums written to a per-group output buffer, correct handling of non-multiple sizes and zero padding. write the file.
prose:
The file wrote successfully. `reduce.comp` is a complete, ready-to-compile GLSL 450 compute shader.

A few things worth noting about the design:

**Non-multiple sizes** — the guard `gid < elementCount` on the load zero-fills any lane whose global index falls past the end of the array, so the reduction math stays clean regardless of input length.

**Tree reduction** — stride starts at 128 (half of 256) and halves each iteration. Each level has a `barrier()` + `memoryBarrierShared()` pair, which is the minimum needed to guarantee visibility before the next read.

**Push constant** — passing `elementCount` as a push constant is the cheapest path; it avoids a buffer read and keeps the descriptor set simple.

**Two-pass pattern** — this shader produces one partial sum per workgroup. You dispatch it with `ceil(N / 256)` workgroups, then either fold the partial sums on the CPU or run a second dispatch of the same shader over the output buffer (which is at most a few thousand floats, so one more workgroup finishes the job).

If you want specialisation constants for `local_size_x` instead of a hard-coded 256, or a single-pass path using subgroup ops (`subgroupAdd` + one elected lane writes the workgroup sum), let me know.
